stories.title: What do we know about the man who tried to shoot Trump?
stories.summary: NPR's Mary Louise Kelly speaks with NPR Justice Correspondent Ryan Lucas and National Security Correspondent Greg Myre about security at the White House Correspondents' Dinner and the war in Iran.

stories.title: 20,000 civilian sailors are stuck in the gulf that opens to the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Thousands of seafarers remain stuck as the Strait of Hormuz blockade continues. The United Nations urges for a plan to facilitate their release.

stories.title: Texas coastal city faces worsening water shortage due to prolonged drought
stories.summary: After years of drought, Corpus Christi, Texas, is on the brink of a water emergency, as freshwater sources have dried up, leaving close to half a million people at risk of not having drinking water.

stories.title: Suicide rates have dropped since the 2022 launch of the 988 line
stories.summary: NPR's Juana Summers talks with Angela Kimball of the mental health advocacy group Inseparable about the drop in suicide rates after the launch of the 988 Lifeline.

stories.title: Will.i.am wants to future-proof a new generation
stories.summary: The Black Eyed Peas co-founder turned entrepreneur is now teaching a class on "agentic AI" for Arizona State.

stories.title: Giving coffee a jolt could help assess its quality
stories.summary: NPR's science podcast Short Wave looks at the secrets behind scorpions' weapons, using electricity to measure the quality of a cup of coffee, and what shapes the content of dreams.
